The results showed that when FA receptors were saturated, the intracellular fluorescent signal of the FA-C6-SLNs group was significantly weakened (almost no fluorescence), indicating that its cellular uptake was effectively inhibited. Even if a single targeting pathway was blocked, efficient cellular uptake could still be achieved through the pathway mediated by the other ligand, significantly improving the reliability of targeted drug delivery.

GA specifically binds to GA receptors highly expressed on hepatocellular carcinoma cells, mediating active targeting uptake and significantly enhancing antitumor activity.
